title: Container stewardship catalog and driver stability harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We lack a single curated surface that ties container images, lightweight SBOM deltas, and validated driver/CUDA bundles into a searchable catalog for release engineers and SREs. This gap causes reactive driver rollbacks and slow rollouts for Dedicated/Private clusters. Goal: build a container stewardship catalog and a driver stability harness that together enable deterministic upgrade gates: (1) catalog image cohorts with provenance fingerprints and delta SBOMs; (2) attach validated driver bundles and hardware-compat labels; (3) run a harness to exercise candidate image+driver pairs through a canary suite and record stability signals for rollout gating. Deliverables should be usable by the runtime team for canary rails and by the infra team to automate safe driver promotions.
acceptance_criteria: A searchable catalog exists that lists images, SBOM delta links, manifest fingerprints, and associated driver bundle versions for each release channel (stable, lts, beta)

Automated harness can deploy image+driver pair to a 3-node canary pool, run the stability suite (KV cache warmup, continuous batching stress, multi-sequence inference), and emit a pass/fail signal and quantitative metrics to the rollout dashboard
Catalog entries include a binary provenance fingerprint (sha512), SBOM delta URL, kernel/driver compatibility notes, and a suggested rollout policy (canary size, observation window)
Rollout gate integration: when harness marks a candidate as failed, the release pipeline blocks promotion and files an incident with root-cause metadata
Documentation and runbook produced: how to onboard a new driver bundle, how to interpret harness metrics, and emergency rollback steps
tasks: Design catalog schema and minimal API (fields: image_tag, image_sha512, sbom_delta_url, driver_bundle_tag, hw_labels, suggested_rollout_policy)
Prototype lightweight SBOM delta generator in the CI pipeline and store artifacts in GCS with signed URLs
Implement driver stability harness: k8s job + tests that exercise inference runtime paths and surface OOMs, kernel panics, and latency regressions
Wire harness outputs into rollout dashboard: metric mapping and failure thresholds
Create a migration plan for existing images to populate initial catalog cohort
Author runbook and handoff notes for oncall and release engineers

2025-03-03 - Security review assigned to Jordan Kim. Preliminary notes: need to sign SBOM deltas and ensure driver bundles are signed; adding to security review checklist.
2025-03-04 - Miguel Santos: Harness baseline run on staging completed (3 runs). One regression detected under stress scenario with driver v510. Filed ENG-18243 for follow-up with driver vendor.
Reviewer feedback: PM requests a short SLA matrix for catalog availability before we rely on it for automated rollouts. Action: add monitoring for catalog health.
notes: Trade-offs considered: storing full SBOMs for every image increases storage and index costs; chose delta SBOMs with on-demand reconstruction. Chose smaller canary pools to reduce cost but increased observation windows to compensate. Future work: integrate HSM-signed driver manifests and add a verification step in the Dedicated provisioning flow.
